title: Bake-off (validators): Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
question: Who stands behind NEAR’s validators? Make me a fresh flower with their backers, not an existing one.
note: A real run on NEAR AI Cloud (T060), kept with the signature each completion got. A hash or link the model copied from a tool result is written as a reference to that result ($from, {{…}}), so it replays on recordedClient.

turns.content: The right network is `near-validators` (readable, has `backers` segments), and no existing flowers for it — so I'll build a fresh one.

Snapshot reused (fixture, final) as of 2026-11-03, block 222,915,356. 371 validators, 593.37M NEAR staked. Now I'll build the spec — the question needs `segments: "backers"`; the rest I'll leave to defaults.

interpretation.summary: This flower shows NEAR's 371 active validators as a ring, each side's bar sized by its current-epoch stake, largest first. Each bar is split into the backer classes that stand behind it: other delegators, accounts holding 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts, and lockups. Stake is concentrated: the top 10 pools hold about 36% and the Nakamoto coefficient is 9.

power_means.claim: Power here is validator stake in the current epoch: how much NEAR is staked to a pool and thus entitles its operator to produce blocks and chunks. Total is about 593.37M NEAR across 371 pools; the top pool (astro-stakers) holds ~5.6%, the top 10 hold ~36.2%, and 9 pools would be needed to reach a third of all stake.

mappings.why: Each side's width is the validator's share of current-epoch stake, compressed into a band so small pools stay visible beside the large ones.
Each bar's height is the square root of that stake share, so a validator's slice stands straight out in proportion to its power.
Colour marks the kind of account (staking pool, liquid-staking contract, or unknown) so the eye can pick out non-pool actors.
A solid outline means the name is self-declared or verified, dashed means inferred, none means unknown; pool names are self-declared in pool-details.near, not verified.
The question asks who stands behind each validator, so each bar is segmented by backer class: other delegators, accounts with 1M+ NEAR, liquid-staking contracts, and lockups.
Validators are ordered largest-stake first, clockwise from the top, so the most powerful pools sit together at the top.

conflicts: Stake is not the only kind of power on NEAR: governance votes (e.g. House of Stake / veNEAR), protocol role, and off-chain influence (exchanges, liquid-staking control of token holders) also matter. This flower draws only staking power and its delegators.
unknowns: Lockup contract owners were not resolved, so 'lockup' backers are opaque to a single controller.

Liquid-staking contracts appear as a backer class, but their own token holders are not listed (would need contract state / token-holder APIs), so we cannot say who really backs e.g. Meta Pool or LiNEAR.

Pool identities are self-declared (pool-details.near); a named .near account is a self-declared identity, not a verified one, and several listed operators (figment, staked, bitwise) have no self-declared identity here.
Idle pools (~424, ~6656 delegation records) were not crawled, so their delegators are missing from the backer breakdown.
Delegations under 1,000 NEAR are folded per pool and class, so small individual backers are grouped rather than named.
inferred: figment.poolv1.near and ledgerbyfigment.poolv1.near may be run by the same operator (Figment), but this is inference from naming, not evidence in the snapshot.

Addresses are holders, not confirmed people.
